claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Severe lattice distortion and chemical complexity in WTaTiVZr activate multiple slip systems and dynamic recovery processes.
The activated deformation processes include twinning and dislocation cross-slip.
These deformation processes refine the dislocation substructure and diffuse stress concentrations.
Refinement of the dislocation substructure and diffusion of stress concentrations blunt cracks during deformation.
The proposed WTaTiVZr specimen is fully dense, homogeneous, and polycrystalline.
Commercially used pure tungsten has a body-centered-cubic crystal structure.
A temperature range of approximately 1000–1200°C is representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
The cocktail effect in WTaTiVZr creates varied local bonding environments and significant lattice strain.
WTaTiVZr has a richer repertoire of deformation mechanisms than pure tungsten.
Limited slip activity and brittle grain boundaries dominate deformation or failure in pure tungsten under the stated conditions.
The active deformation mechanisms in WTaTiVZr facilitate stress relaxation and delay crack initiation and propagation at high temperature.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will absorb more deformation energy than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will show more multiple-slip activity, dynamic recovery, twinning, and crack blunting than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten will show more brittle fracture behavior than WTaTiVZr under the same high-temperature conditions.
The proposed advantage of WTaTiVZr is expected to be most pronounced at approximately 1000–1200°C.
At substantially lower temperatures, reduced activation of recovery mechanisms may diminish the difference between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
The proposed effect requires WTaTiVZr to retain a homogeneous microstructure without significant processing defects.
